knowledge:
- key_parameters: filename=Path to a pathway file, a vector of files, or a directory containing files ;; parse.as=Whether to parse the network as "metabolic" (default, bipartite) or "signaling" (protein-protein interaction) ;; miriam=Specifies which MIRIAM annotation attributes to extract (e.g., "all", "go") ;; simplify=In makeReactionNetwork, whether to remove reaction vertices missing gene annotations ;; weight.method=Method to compute edge weights from expression data (e.g., "cor" for Pearson correlation) ;; use.attr=The vertex attribute matching the microarray features (e.g., "miriam.affy.probeset", "miriam.uniprot") ;; method=Path ranking method, either "prob.shortest.path" (ECDF-based shortest path) or "pvalue" (comparison against random paths) ;; M=Number of clusters or components for path clustering/classification ;; target.class=The sample category to classify in pathClassifier
- alternatives: rBiopaxParser is required to parse BioPAX files instead of KGML/SBML; RCurl is used to fetch online annotations from BridgeDb; igraph is used for network representation, but networks can be converted to Bioconductor's graphNEL using toGraphNEL for integration with the graph package
- when_to_use: Use when you have genome-scale pathway files (KEGG, Reactome, BioModels) and matching transcriptomic/microarray data, and you want to identify, rank, cluster, or classify active metabolic or signaling paths associated with specific phenotypes
- pitfalls: SBML2igraph requires libSBML to be installed on the system during package installation, which is not supported out-of-the-box on Windows Bioconductor; fetchAttribute requires an active internet connection to query BridgeDb; reaction networks often contain translocation or spontaneous reactions lacking gene annotations, which should be filtered using simplifyReactionNetwork or makeReactionNetwork(..., simplify=TRUE) to avoid downstream weighting issues

workflows.name: network_path_mining
workflows.intent: Construct a network from pathway files, convert it to a reaction or gene network, weight it with gene expression data, rank active paths, and cluster/classify them.
input: pathway_file.xml (KGML, SBML, or BioPAX pathway file)
expression_data.txt (Gene expression matrix, e.g., microarray expression matrix)
workflows.stages: 1. Parse pathway files into an igraph network ;; 2. Convert bipartite metabolic network to reaction or gene network representations ;; 3. Fetch missing annotations from BridgeDb (optional) ;; 4. Assign edge weights based on gene expression correlation ;; 5. Rank paths using probabilistic shortest path or p-value methods ;; 6. Cluster and classify paths to identify biomarkers ;; 7. Visualize networks, paths, and clusters
workflows.code:
# Database Extraction
graph <- KGML2igraph(filename = file)
graph <- SBML2igraph(filename = file)

library(rBiopaxParser)
biopax = readBiopax(file)
graph <- BioPAX2igraph(biopax = biopax)

graph <- KGML2igraph(filename = c(file1, file2))
graph <- KGML2igraph(filename = ".")

graph <- SBML2igraph(filename = file, miriam = "all")
graph <- BioPAX2igraph(biopax = biopax, miriam = "go")

graph <- KGML2igraph(filename = file, parse.as = "signaling")
graph <- KGML2igraph(filename = file, parse.as = "signaling", expand.complexes = TRUE)

# Network Processing
rgraph <- makeReactionNetwork(graph, simplify=FALSE)
rgraph <- simplifyReactionNetwork(rgraph)
rgraph <- makeReactionNetwork(graph, simplify=TRUE)

ggraph <- expandComplexes(rgraph, v.attr = "miriam.uniprot", keep.parent.attr= c("^pathway", "^compartment"))
ggraph <- makeGeneNetwork(rgraph)

# Weighting Network
rgraph <- fetchAttribute(rgraph, organism = "Homo sapiens", target.attr = "miriam.affy.probeset", source.attr = "miriam.uniprot")

library(ALL)
data(ALL)
rgraph <- assignEdgeWeights(microarray = exprs(ALL), graph = rgraph, weight.method = "cor", use.attr="miriam.affy.probeset", y=ALL$mol.bio, bootstrap = FALSE)

# Path Ranking
ranked.p <- pathRanker(rgraph, method = "prob.shortest.path", K = 25, minPathSize = 6)

pathsample <- samplePaths(rgraph, max.path.length = vcount(rgraph), num.samples = 1000, num.warmup = 10)
ranked.p <- pathRanker(rgraph, method = "pvalue", sampledpaths = pathsample ,alpha=0.1)

eids <- getPathsAsEIDs(paths = ranked.p, graph = rgraph)
eids <- getPathsAsEIDs(paths = ranked.p, graph = ggraph)

# Clustering and classification of paths
ybinpaths <- pathsToBinary(ranked.p)
p.cluster <- pathCluster(ybinpaths, M = 2)
plotClusters(ybinpaths, p.cluster)

p.class <- pathClassifier(ybinpaths, target.class = "BCR/ABL", M = 2)
plotClassifierROC(p.class)
plotClusters(ybinpaths, p.class)

# Plotting
plotNetwork(rgraph, vertex.color="compartment.name")
plotPaths(ranked.p, rgraph)
plotPaths(ranked.p, graph, path.clusters=p.class)

plotAllNetworks(ranked.p, metabolic.net = graph, reaction.net = rgraph, path.clusters=p.class, vertex.label = "", vertex.size = 4)

layout.c <- clusterVertexByAttr(rgraph, "pathway", cluster.strength = 3)
v.color <- colorVertexByAttr(rgraph, "pathway")
plotPaths(ranked.p , rgraph, clusters=p.class, layout = layout.c, vertex.color = v.color)

plotCytoscapeGML(graph, file="example.gml", layout = layout.c, vertex.size = 5, vertex.color = v.color)
